topic: What D-39's evidence leaves out for the user (usability)
detail: Operator-scope memory reads under a policy need evidence of the user (SP-025): a caller in its terminal's foreground process group, reached from that group's leader (or the shell that started it) without passing launchd, whose leader is no harness; or Orch.app at /Applications or ~/Applications. The user's own scripts run from launchd or cron, a development build of Orch.app outside those folders, a command in a pipeline whose first command already exited, and any call whose process group leader cannot be read get public memory only. Accept as documented, or widen once RC-705 and RC-706 settle what counts as evidence. The security limits of the evidence are RC-705 and RC-706.
note: Superseded by D-71 (2026-11-14): terminals are no longer evidence under a policy, so the usability limits listed here no longer apply; terminal access returns with SP-077's unlock.
